en.heading: 23 July: Apolinario Mabini Day and its city-specific rule
en.origin: The day honours Apolinario Mabini, a leader of the Philippine independence movement born on 23 July 1864 in Tanauan. en.heading: 3 April: the award protecting Philippine living cultural treasures
en.origin: The Gawad sa Manlilikha ng Bayan recognizes masters of traditional Filipino arts who have transmitted skills to their communities, including weaving, carving, performance and other living practices. Republic Act No. 7355, approved 3 April 1992, established recognition of national living treasures and mechanisms for safeguarding and passing on traditional folk arts to later generations. The Honors Code introduced by Executive Order No. 236 in 2003 later placed this award within the hierarchy of national distinctions. The award's 1992 founding differs from the NCCA establishment under separate RA 7356 on the same date.

en.heading: 18 December: Graciano López Jaena and a nationwide working holiday
en.origin: Graciano López Jaena Day remembers the Filipino writer and reform advocate associated with La Solidaridad. It falls on 18 December, the birth anniversary of a figure in the country's nineteenth-century reform movement. Earlier proclamations, including Proclamation No. 52 of December 1986, granted a special non-working day in Iloilo for that particular year's celebrations, but did not establish permanent nationwide time off. Republic Act No. 9070, approved 8 April 2001, set 18 December annually as a special working public holiday throughout the Philippines. This national classification is different from the older one-off local non-working proclamations.

en.heading: 19 February: Jose Abad Santos Day has more than one historic date
en.origin: Jose Abad Santos Day honours a Filipino jurist and Chief Justice remembered for refusing to cooperate with occupying Japanese forces during the Second World War. The official date is tied to his birth on 19 February 1886. Proclamation No. 128 of 1949 had used 15 May; Proclamation No. 374, signed 26 December 1956, moved the annual commemoration to 19 February so schools could participate outside summer vacation. Proclamation No. 229 reaffirmed 19 February annually in January 2000. Separately, Republic Act No. 8815 of August 2000 lists a special non-working day on 7 May in Pampanga and Angeles City; that local rule must not be silently substituted for the national 19 February commemoration.

La Proclamazione n. 229 ribadì il 19 febbraio nel gennaio 2000. Separatamente, la Legge n. 8815 dell'agosto 2000 indica il 7 maggio come festività speciale non lavorativa a Pampanga e Angeles City: la norma locale non sostituisce il 19 febbraio nazionale.
